name: Almanac X Alcron Prague
insider_take: Art Deco elegance meets Michelin-starred dining in the heart of Old Town Prague.
whats_special: The Alcron is home to Prague's first Michelin-starred restaurant, helmed by acclaimed chef Roman Paulus. This beautifully restored 1930s Art Deco gem sits just steps from Wenceslas Square, where the Velvet Revolution transformed history in 1989. The hotel's name pays homage to the original Alcron restaurant, once a legendary gathering place for Prague's elite.
pro_tip: Book the Alcron restaurant's tasting menu well in advance - it's Prague's only Michelin star and tables fill up quickly, especially for the chef's signature seafood preparations.
dont_miss: The stunning original Art Deco elevator and lobby details, plus the hotel's prime location means you're a 5-minute walk to the famous Astronomical Clock and Prague Castle views. The rooftop terrace offers incredible sunset views over the red-tiled roofs of Lesser Town.
pros: Historic luxury hotel with Art Deco elegance in Prague's city center
Michelin-starred Alcron Restaurant offering exceptional fine dining
Prime location near Wenceslas Square and major attractions
Sophisticated rooms and suites with premium amenities
cons: Historic building may have smaller room sizes than modern hotels
